newsitem.title: ROMANIA: MobiFon says to invest $500 mln in Romania GSM.
newsitem.headline: MobiFon says to invest $500 mln in Romania GSM.

text.p: AirTouch of the U.S. and Canada's Telesystem International Wireless (TIW), which won a licence for a GSM cellular phone system in Romania this week, said they would invest $500 million in the project.
On Friday, the Communications Ministry said the MobiFon consortium, led by Airtouch Communications Inc and TIW, had won one of the two licences offered in a tender.
The other winner was the MobilRom consortium, led by France Telecom, it said.
A MobiFon statement said the consortium would invest the $500 million over the next 10 years. The investment was expected to create over 1,000 new jobs, it added.

Romania's Posta Romana post authority and local private firms Logic Telecom SA data network operator, Ana Elecronic consUmer electronics retailer, ISAF engineering company and the Romanian Investment Fund are also part of the consortium.

The licence has a ten-year validity and requires the winning companies to cover with the new GSM digital system -- within the next 18 months of winning the tender -- Romania's main cities as well as to provide GSM coverage along European transit routes in Romania.
Frequency concession tax amounts to $50 million per licence and operators would be charged a fee of $5 million per year of operation. The inital number of channels per operator is 22.

Ex-communist Romania is the last state in the region to set up a digital GSM system. It currently operates an analogue technology mobile phone network covering eight cities, in partnership with Telefonica de Espana SA.

"Romania's 23 million people, when combined with the low cellular and landline penetration rates and an economy that has been making progress, all adds up to a market that is both very attractive to us," the MobiFon statement said. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
